translation.text: And they completed these things by the decree of the Lord, the God of Israel, and with the approval[a] of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of the Persians[b].

footnotes.text: Or 'with the consent' or 'in accordance with the decision' of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes.

Greek main text: 'king of the Persians,' singular, formally following Artaxerxes. The existing English plural treats the title distributively across the named rulers; alternatively, 'Artaxerxes, king of the Persians.'

lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb denotes bringing something to its intended end. 'Completed' is natural English and fits the context of finishing the temple-related work without overinterpreting the scope.
The plural demonstrative is explicit in Greek. 'These things' preserves the broader reference to the matters just described; 'these works' would be interpretive, though contextually plausible.

The printed form προστάγματος is the genitive of πρόσταγμα. The consulted entry supports an authoritative ordinance/command sense, so the existing decree wording is retained. This corrects the modern import's missing sigma, not an ancient variant.

lexical_decisions.chosen: of the Lord, the God of Israel
alternatives: of the Lord God of Israel
lexical_decisions.rationale: κύριος is rendered 'Lord' per project doctrine. The appositional phrase 'the God of Israel' is kept explicit for clarity and fidelity to the Greek.

γνώμη can mean opinion, intention, resolve, or approval. In this administrative context, referring to Persian kings, 'with the approval' best captures official concurrence. It also aligns with the sense that divine decree and royal authorization both stand behind the work.
Personal names are transliterated by standard English conventions, following project policy.

The selected printed main body has singular βασιλέως, king of the Persians, formally following Artaxerxes. The existing English plural is retained as a distributive interpretation of the coordinated royal names, not a claim that the main-body Greek is plural; the singular alternative is explicit in the note. This narrow import repair does not newly establish that distributive interpretation.

theological_decisions.issue: Relationship between divine causation and imperial authorization
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: The verse presents the completion as occurring both by the Lord's decree and with the approval of Persian rulers.
alternative_readings: The royal approval could be read as subordinate explanation of the divine decree alone.
The phrase 'king of the Persians' may be taken distributively over all three names rather than syntactically with Artaxerxes alone.
theological_decisions.rationale: The Greek coordinates διὰ προστάγματος ... καὶ μετὰ τῆς γνώμης .... Retain the existing divine-decree and royal-approval wording without collapsing the two constructions. The main English plural royal title is an interpretive retention, qualified by the note, not the morphology of the printed singular.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: DOCTRINE.md: Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it

4.routing_rationale: No clause movement or main wording change apart from marker placement. Correct the lexical noun and matching theological quotation to printed προστάγματος; anchor the approval note to approval and the singular-title note to the English royal title. Preserve the existing distributive plural as qualified interpretation, not Greek morphology.

translation.text: And the sons of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, and the rest from the captivity[a] who had been added[b], did according to what is in the book of Moses.

footnotes.text: Or 'from the exile' for 'from the captivity'.
Or, idiomatically, 'who had joined them.' Greek: 'who had been added'; it does not explicitly state the agent or to whom they were added.

lexical_decisions.rationale: A formally close rendering preserves the stock biblical expression. Although 'Israelites' is smoother modern English, 'sons of Israel' reflects the Greek wording and keeps continuity with the traditional ethnic-covenantal designation.
'The rest' is the most natural concise rendering for the substantival adjective here, distinguishing this group from priests and Levites already named.

The Greek literally refers to those associated with the captivity/exile. 'From the captivity' stays close to the wording, while the sense is effectively 'from the exile.' The alternative is preserved because modern readers may find it clearer.

The checked printed word is an aorist passive participle of προστίθημι. The entry's addition sense supports added; its joining uses help explain the idiomatic alternative but do not turn this passive into an explicit active return verb. The agent and the complement of added are not stated. Prefer the close passive provisionally, with the joined formulation in a note; do not identify a precise admission event or infer a Hebrew Vorlage.

Together with the following dative phrase, the adverb expresses conformity to the Mosaic-book standard. Match the existing main English according to rather than the stale chosen field accordingly; no change to the main clause is needed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: what is in the book of Moses
alternatives: according to the things in the book of Moses
to the prescriptions in the book of Moses
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase supplies the standard governed by according to in the main wording. Retain book rather than inserting an unexpressed law noun.

theological_decisions.issue: Agency and group identification in οἱ προστεθέντες
theological_decisions.rationale: The corrected printed passive leaves the agent and complement unstated. The candidate keeps that openness and offers an idiomatic joined alternative without making an explicit return journey, divine admission, conversion or a particular admission event part of the main text. The old brought-back/returned explanation belongs to the superseded imported-word record, not an attested ancient alternative established here.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: DOCTRINE.md: optimal equivalence; source distinctions; preserve ambiguity and document alternatives.

6.routing_rationale: No boundary move. Replace only the consequential participial English, align its active lexical/theological fields with προστεθέντες, and reanchor captivity and participle notes to their own terms. Remove obsolete brought-back gloss and the unverified WLC-parallel claim. Other main English choices remain; ἀκολούθως metadata now matches the already-existing according to wording.
